name: com.mathproven/tools
title: Mathproven
description: State rules and rates from sourced tables, each row with its citation, source and date read.

tools.name: list_tables
tools.description: Lists Mathproven's sourced reference tables of state rules and rates (bookkeeping, construction, crypto, ecommerce, insurance, law firms, nonprofits, property management and trucking): each table's name, what it holds, how its members are named, how many have a row, and its page. Use it to find the table name that read_table and table_findings take. It takes no input.

tools.name: read_table
tools.description: Reads one member's row of a Mathproven reference table (a state's figure, for example) for a date: the figures in plain words, each row's citation, official source address and the day it was read, and the table's certificate. A member with no row is answered as not covered, with the reason, never as a zero. Use it when someone asks for a state's rule, rate, threshold, period or deadline that one of the tables holds. It takes only a table name, a member's code and a date: no amounts, names or files.

table.description: The table's name, as list_tables gives it (for example "fuel-tax-rates-third-quarter-2026").

member.description: The member's code: a state's two-letter postal code (OH) or DC; for the fuel tax table a member jurisdiction's code, Canadian provinces included (ON); for the capital gains table a filing status (S, MFJ, MFS, HOH) or a tax year and status (2026-MFJ).

date.description: Optional. The day the answer is for, written YYYY-MM-DD (a policy effective date for the stamping fee table). Without it, today's date (UTC).

tools.name: table_findings
tools.description: Gives what a Mathproven reference table shows as a whole: its findings (counts, ranges and the most common figure, worked out from its rows and checked a second way, where the table's page shows them), how many members have a row and which do not, and its certificate. Use it for a question about a table as a whole, such as how many states set a figure or the range of the rates. It takes only a table name.

table.description: The table's name, as list_tables gives it (for example "fuel-tax-rates-third-quarter-2026").
